sections.heading: Where the Dust Lies to You
paras: The dust has a story about eternal life, and it sounds like a pension. You put in your seventy years. You keep your record as clean as a working man can keep it. If the numbers hold, there is a payout on the far side of the grave. Until then, life is the grind — the alarm, the back that hurts, the bills on the counter — and God is somewhere up the road waiting to see how you finish.

Folded inside that lie is a second one. It tells you God is someone to know about, not someone to know. You can learn His rules the way you learn a foreman’s habits — what sets Him off, what keeps Him quiet. So faith turns into chores. Church on Sunday, grace before supper, a few dollars in the plate. A man can do all of that for forty years and never once speak to God the way a son speaks to his father.

Live under both lies long enough and the ground gives back nothing but more dust. Ask that man on a bad night how his soul is, and if he tells you the truth, he will tell it in the psalmist’s words: My soul clings to the dust; Revive me according to Your word. (NKJV) To revive is to give life. The psalm asks for it now, not later, and it asks for it by a word.

John 17 gives that word, and it comes from the mouth of the Son as He talks to His Father: This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ. Life is not a payout after the funeral. It is knowing God through His Son, and it starts the day you believe.

sections.heading: The Last Words Before the Garden
pulls: The dust says eternal life is a pension paid out after the grave to men whose records hold. Jesus says it is knowing the only true God through the Son He sent — and it starts the day you believe.
paras: Part Three ended on the last night, with Jesus telling eleven frightened men that trouble was coming and why they could take heart: I have overcome the world. Soon He will walk out over the brook Kidron to a garden Judas knew well. Before He goes, He prays. This last volume of the series opens there, with the Son talking to His Father.

He prays out loud, with His men listening. He says so Himself: I say these things in the world, that they may have my joy made full in themselves. The prayer moves in three steps — for Himself, for the eleven, and for everyone who will believe through their word. This week takes the first five verses. The Son asks for glory with the cross less than a day off, and in the middle of the asking He tells you, in one sentence, what eternal life is.

parts.label: PART ONE
parts.heading: THE TIME HAS COME
paras: Jesus said these things, then lifting up his eyes to heaven. He looks up. He did the same at Lazarus’ grave, and there He told His Father, I know that you always listen to me. He speaks as the Son to the Father who has never once turned Him away.

Father, the time has come. The whole Gospel has been leaning toward this sentence. At the wedding in Cana He said, My hour has not yet come. In the temple men tried to seize Him, and no one could, because his hour had not yet come. When the Greeks came asking for Him, He said, The time has come for the Son of Man to be glorified. Now the supper is over and the betrayer is gone. The hour is the cross, and it is here.

Glorify your Son, that your Son may also glorify you. Do not hear this as a man asking for his name on a sign. The Son is asking to be lifted up — onto the cross, out of the tomb, home to the Father — so that the Father would be seen for who He is. The glory of the Son and the glory of the Father are one glory. There is nothing grasping in it.

The hour came on schedule. No mob rushed it. No fear of the Son pushed it back. The Father set it before the world began, and the Son walked into it with His eyes open. Your rescue was not an accident of politics or a plan that went wrong. It was the hour.

parts.label: PART TWO
parts.heading: AUTHORITY OVER ALL FLESH
paras: Even as you gave him authority over all flesh, so he will give eternal life to all whom you have given him. Within hours Jesus will be bound and led from one court to another. Yet He speaks as One who has authority over every man who draws breath — over Annas, over Pilate, over the soldiers with their torches, and over you. All flesh means every son of Adam, every man made from the dust of the ground.

Watch what He does with that authority. A man with power over others usually takes something. He takes wages, land, a cut, a little more respect than he is owed. This King gives. The authority the Father handed Him is authority to give eternal life. He does not hold it over your head. He holds it out.

All whom you have given him. That phrase will come back again and again in this prayer. The Father gives a people to the Son, and the Son gives them life. Jesus said it plainly in Capernaum: All those whom the Father gives me will come to me. He who comes to me I will in no way throw out. God’s choosing is not cold. It is the Father giving a gift to His Son — and you were in the gift.

So your faith in Christ is the sign you were given, never the price you paid for life. You came because the Father gave you and the Son called you. That is why the life He gives cannot be taken back. It never rested on your grip. It rests on the Father’s gift and the Son’s word, and neither of those has ever failed a man.

parts.label: PART THREE
parts.heading: TO KNOW THE ONLY TRUE GOD
pulls: The Son spoke of His work as accomplished the night before the cross. He was that sure of finishing it. Whatever you are still trying to add, He has already called done.
paras: This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ. Here Jesus tells you what eternal life is. He does not begin with length of years, though it has no end. He does not begin with a place, though there is a place. He begins with knowing.

There is a difference between knowing about a man and knowing him. You can know the name, the job, and the truck of the man down the road. You know your wife of thirty years another way — her silences, her laugh, the look she gives when you are about to say something foolish. Jesus means the second kind. Eternal life is to know God as a son knows his father, and to be known by Him.

The only true God. Not one god among many on the shelf. The real one, the living one. Everything else a man bows to is a carving, however it is dressed. And him whom you sent, Jesus Christ. Jesus sets Himself in the same breath as the Father. No prophet would dare, and no mere man could. There is no knowing the Father apart from the Son. No one has seen God at any time. The one and only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has declared him. If you want to know what God is like, look at Jesus.

And it begins now. He who believes in me has eternal life. That is present tense. The day you believed, it started. You will still bury people you love, and one day they will bury you, but the grave will not interrupt it.

parts.label: PART FOUR
parts.heading: THE WORK DONE ON THE EARTH
paras: I glorified you on the earth. I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do. Hear when He says it. The arrest has not happened yet. The cross is still ahead. And the Son speaks of His work as done. He is that sure He will finish it. Before the next sundown He will say it again from the cross, and that word gets its own week.

Think of what He did on the earth. He lived every hour of His life in His Father’s will. He told His men at the well, My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to accomplish his work. He kept the law you broke. He loved the Father with all His heart, every day, without one slip. Where the first man failed in a garden, this Man obeyed, and He is about to walk into another garden to finish it.

Now, Father, glorify me with your own self with the glory which I had with you before the world existed. Before there was any dust, the Word was with God. He set that glory aside to come down into the dirt with you. Now He asks to go home to it.

And here is your hope. The One who goes back to that glory does not leave His flesh behind. The Word became flesh and remains a Man. A Man with your nature, with wounds in His hands, now stands in the glory of the Father. What He finished on the earth, He did for dust men. You do not add to it. You rest on it.

stations.verse: Jesus said these things, then lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said, “Father, the time has come. Glorify your Son, that your Son may also glorify you.
stations.question: With the cross a day away, Jesus lifted His eyes and said, Father, the time has come. Glorify your Son; what does it do to my shame over my sin to know He met that hour as His glory, not His defeat?
stations.gloss: an hour; a set time or season
body: Hōra can name a season set by nature, a part of the day, or an hour. From there it comes to mean a fixed point in time — a moment that belongs to someone. It turns up in ninety-nine verses. Here the WEB renders it the time has come.

John uses it like a drumbeat. At Cana Jesus says, My hour has not yet come. In the temple no one could lay a hand on Him, because his hour had not yet come. Then, days before the end: The time has come for the Son of Man to be glorified. The hour is the cross.

The dust says your life is a string of accidents and the worst day in history was one more of them. Jesus speaks of an hour that was set and kept. No mob moved it early. The hour that saved you came on the Father’s clock.
stations.live: When a hard hour comes this week — the phone call, the bad report, the bill you cannot pay — read John 17:1 before you do anything else. Then say it: ‘The Father kept His hour for my rescue. He holds this one too.’

stations.verse: This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ.
stations.question: Jesus said eternal life is to know you, the only true God; what have I leaned on this year for life and safety as though it could stand beside Him?
stations.gloss: alone; only, the one and no other
body: Monos means alone — by oneself, solitary, even forsaken. Set beside a noun, it means only: this one and no other. It stands in one hundred nine verses. More than once it is joined to God in praise, as when Paul gives glory to God who alone is wise.

John used it earlier that same night. Jesus told the eleven they would scatter, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me. The Son who was about to be left alone by every friend now calls on the only true God — the One who had never left Him.

The dust says God is one choice on a shelf, and a careful man keeps a few others in stock: the savings account, the good name, the second drink. Monos clears the shelf. There is one God. And the only God is the One who sent His Son for you.
stations.live: Name the thing you reach for when you are afraid — the late-night screen, the bottle, a man’s good opinion. Each time you reach for it this week, say: ‘There is one true God, and this is not Him.’

stations.verse: This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ.
stations.question: Jesus defined eternal life as that they should know you, the only true God — the real God, known and not just learned about; what do my prayers this month show about how well I know Him?
stations.gloss: true; real, genuine
body: Alēthinos means true in the sense of real or genuine — the thing itself, not the copy. Twenty-six verses of the New Testament use it, and John reaches for it often. He writes of the true light, of the true bread out of heaven, and Jesus says, I am the true vine.

Each time, the true thing stands beside something that looked like it and was not. So here. The Father is the real God, and every other god is a carving. Paul writes of men who turned to God from idols, to serve a living and true God. John closes his first letter on the same note: This is the true God and eternal life.
The dust keeps handing you counterfeits and calling them gods. They promise life and pay in ash. The true God gives what no copy can. He gives Himself, known through His Son.
stations.live: Read John 1:9, 6:32 and 15:1, one each morning this week. After each, write one line naming the copy you have leaned on in its place. Then write under it: ‘Jesus is the true one.’

stations.verse: This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ.
stations.question: Jesus set Himself beside the Father in one sentence — and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ; where am I trying to reach God by some other road than the Son the Father sent?
stations.gloss: to send out with a commission
body: Apostellō means to send off, and especially to send with a commission — a man sent on business for the one who sent him, carrying his authority. It appears in one hundred thirty verses.

Six verses of this one prayer use it. In each the Father sends the Son, and in one the Son sends His men the same way. He did not come down on His own errand. He came on His Father’s. John says it again in his letter: God has sent his one and only Son into the world that we might live through him.

The dust says God waits at the top of the hill for you to climb up to Him. Apostellō says He sent. He came down the hill Himself, in His Son. And the Sent One now sends: As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.
stations.live: Before you leave the house each day this week, say it out loud: ‘The Father sent His Son for me. The Son sends me into this day.’ Then go to work as a man on His errand.

stations.verse: I glorified you on the earth. I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do.
stations.question: The night before the cross, Jesus told the Father, I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do; what have I been trying to add to that work, as if He had left it unfinished?
stations.gloss: the earth; land, soil, the ground
body: Gē is the plain word for the earth — the world set against heaven, the land set against the sea, the soil a farmer works, the ground under a man’s feet. It is used in two hundred twenty-one verses. The same word names the whole earth and the dirt in a furrow.

John uses it of the dirt. Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. He uses it of the cross: if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself. Jesus did His Father’s work down here — on roads, at a well, beside a grave.

The dust says God works somewhere far above your life, a long way from wages and weather. But the Son glorified His Father on the earth, in a body of flesh, and finished the work on the ground. That is where you were saved.
stations.live: Pick up a handful of dirt this week — from the garden, the field, the edge of the gravel drive. Hold it a minute and say: ‘He finished the Father’s work on this ground, and He did it for me.’

practices.title: PRAY HIS PRAYER BACK
practices.body: Each morning this week, before you pick up the phone, read John 17:1–5 aloud. Then take verse 3 and pray it back to the Father in your own words. Thank Him that eternal life is knowing Him. Ask to know Him better today than yesterday. Keep it short and keep it honest. You are not filing a report with a boss. You are a son talking to the Father whom the Son has made known.

practices.title: CLEAR THE SHELF
practices.body: Jesus calls His Father the only true God. Write down the two or three things you run to for safety when the week goes bad — the overtime, the drink, the praise of the men you work beside. Bring that list to God and name each one as a rival. Confess it plainly. Then tear the paper up and throw it in the burn barrel. The only true God does not share His place, and He does not need to.

practices.title: LOOK AT THE ONE HE SENT
practices.body: You come to know the Father by looking at the Son He sent. Read one chapter from John 1–16 each day this week, the ground this series has already walked. After each, write one sentence about what that chapter shows you of the Father through Jesus — what He loves, what He does with sinners, what He will not let go of. Know Him from His own account, not from rumor or from the God you were afraid of as a boy.

practices.title: STOP ADDING TO THE WORK
practices.body: Jesus said, I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do. Name the thing you keep doing to make yourself right with God — the penance of silence after a bad week, the promise you renew every Monday, the extra hours meant to balance the books. Stop doing it for that reason. Thank Him that the work is done. Then do the good you are called to as a son, not as a debtor.

practices.title: KNOW HIM ON A WEEKDAY
practices.body: Eternal life starts the day a man believes. It is not on hold until the funeral. So pick one ordinary stretch of time this week — the drive in, the lunch break, the walk out to the barn — and spend it with God on purpose. Talk to Him. Read a few verses and think on them. A man who already has eternal life can know God on the earth, in the dirt, on a Wednesday.

title: This Is Eternal Life
subtitle: from dust to knowing the only true God
keyVerse: This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ.

passage.text: Jesus said these things, then lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said, “Father, the time has come. Glorify your Son, that your Son may also glorify you;
even as you gave him authority over all flesh, so he will give eternal life to all whom you have given him.
This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ.
I glorified you on the earth. I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do.
Now, Father, glorify me with your own self with the glory which I had with you before the world existed.

stationsIntro: Read these verses as a man overhearing the Son talk to His Father on the last night. Answer plainly, then let each Greek word show you a little more of what He asked for and what He gave.
lifeIntro: The Father gave a people to His Son, and the Son gives them eternal life. He came to the earth, did every bit of the work, and asked to go home to the glory He had before the world began. These practices rest on that. They are ways for a man who has been given life to spend this week knowing the God who gave it.
lifePulls: Eternal life is not a payout waiting on the far side of the grave. It is knowing the only true God through the Son He sent — and the Son has already finished the work that makes it yours.
prayer: Father, Your Son lifted His eyes to You on the night before the cross. Thank You that the hour came when You set it, and that He walked into it on purpose for me. Thank You that You gave me to Him, and that He gives eternal life to all You have given Him. Teach me to know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You sent. Forgive me for the gods of dust I have reached for when I was afraid. Thank You that Jesus glorified You on the earth and finished the work You gave Him to do. Keep me from adding my work to His, and let me rest my whole weight on what He has done. Let me live today as a man who already has eternal life. In Jesus’ name, amen.
